decisions.inv1_semantics: User-selected: the trusted source is the registered worktree that currently has git.target_branch checked out. Whether that checkout is the physical primary repo or a linked worktree does NOT affect the verdict; every other worktree is still refused. The rejected alternative was to additionally require it be an explicitly configured checkout -- narrower, but it needs a new config key and a misconfiguration would deadlock the tooling exactly as today.
decisions.existing_tests: User-approved earlier, and corrected after brief-r3 flagged the wording: the 17 guards in tests/test_worktree_detection.py are NOT read-only. They may receive premise-preserving rewrites under INV-4, each justified line by line, with no attack shape weakened. The three other test files (test_preflight_status_source.py, test_finalize_merge_first_call.py, test_finalize_merge_toctou.py) may receive minimal, individually justified adjustment.
decisions.flow: User-selected: brief second signature BEFORE dispatching any implementation. The WP-03 experience is that specification defects are cheapest to catch at this gate.
decisions.anchor: User-selected after brief-r2: the trusted branch anchor must live OUTSIDE the repository write domain. rev3 uses $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/agentic_loop/policy.toml (default $HOME/.config/...) key [trust] protected_branch, measured to be inside no git worktree. Rejected, each measured: .agentic/config.toml (git TRACKED), refs/remotes/origin/HEAD (movable by one local symbolic-ref call), server ls-remote (remote.origin.url is locally rewritable, plus a network dependency), environment variable (caller-declared fact -- the A22 bypass family).
decisions.literal_defect: [SUPERSEDED by scope_rev5 at brief rev5/rev6 -- merge.sh and gate/qoder_security.py are now ALLOWED, because WP-02 merged both into the single predicate and WP-01 faces five call sites, not three. Original note kept for history:] User-selected: the pre-existing INV-5 violation in merge.sh:37 and qoder_security.py:1012 (literal '/.worktrees/' instead of the hardened predicate) is fixed by a SEPARATE WP. decisions.direction_c: User-selected after three REWORKs in one root-cause family: option (c). WP-01 is DOWNGRADED to a pure usability fix. It resolves the finalize/preflight/merge deadlock and explicitly WITHDRAWS any claim of defending against a malicious LOCAL actor. Rationale accepted from the escalation: in this threat model anyone who can write the repository or set the caller's environment can already modify the code itself, so an unmovable local trust root is a false goal, whereas the deadlock is a real daily obstruction. Every anchor attempt is therefore abandoned: rev1 (status field), rev2 (origin/HEAD + tracked config), rev3 (XDG_CONFIG_HOME policy file) are all superseded.
decisions.wp02_split: [SUPERSEDED by scope_rev5 at brief rev5/rev6 -- merge.sh and gate/qoder_security.py are now ALLOWED, because WP-02 merged both into the single predicate and WP-01 faces five call sites, not three. Original note kept for history:] User-selected: the pre-existing literal-path defect (wrappers/merge.sh:37 and gate/qoder_security.py:1012 testing the '/.worktrees/' fragment instead of the hardened predicate) is fixed FIRST, in its own WP-02, because it is independent of the trust-root question and is a live INV-5 violation. Those two files are removed from WP-01's allowed_paths and remain forbidden here.
decisions.scope_rev5: D13 closed. brief section 6 and status forbidden_paths previously contradicted each other on merge.sh and gate/qoder_security.py: the brief allowed them, the status forbade them. WP-02 merged both into the single predicate, so WP-01 must be able to edit them -- there are FIVE call sites, not three. finalize_merge.sh was missing from allowed_paths entirely despite being one of the original three. Flagged by topo-brief-r4 Q2.

findings: D1 (fatal, orchestrator-reproduced): rev1 had the predicate read git.target_branch from the status file, but that field exists ONLY in the PLAN schema. Measured -- WP template git keys: base_branch, base_commit, branch, commit, dispatch_commit, worktree. Four of the five call sites validate a WP status, so rev1 required reading a field that does not exist on the object being validated: not implementable.

D2: even if the field existed it comes from the file under validation, so an attacker checking out feat/evil in their own worktree and writing that name into the status satisfies all three rev1 conjuncts and becomes the trusted source. rev2 moves the expected branch to an EXTERNAL dual anchor (origin/HEAD with the origin/ prefix stripped, plus a new [project] protected_branch config key) that must agree byte-for-byte; a status field may only cross-check, never override.

D3 (orchestrator-reproduced): rev1's 'all 17 guards stay green read-only' is impossible -- all 17 call path_is_in_worktree(path) with a SINGLE argument and cannot pass a target branch, and their assertions encode the premise 'every linked worktree is refused' that the new contract deliberately changes. rev2 replaces it with 'the attack guarantees are preserved, the assertions may be rewritten premise-preserving' plus a mandatory 17-row old-node-to-new-assertion mapping.

Q1 CONFIRMED BY ORCHESTRATOR MEASUREMENT: the dual anchor is not a real trust boundary. Both anchors sit in the same write domain -- a single local `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD refs/remotes/origin/<evil>` moves anchor 1 with no server, push or approval involved (reproduced in /tmp/anchprobe), and anchor 2 is a tracked file in the same tree. An actor who can commit moves both in one step and keeps them byte-identical. rev2's security claim ('two sources in the same trust domain constitute an independent anchor') must be withdrawn.

Q2 BLOCKING DEFECT A (scope self-contradiction): the brief's scope permits adding [project] protected_branch to .agentic/config.toml, but this frozen status still lists that file under forbidden_paths. Any implementation would be out of scope on its first edit.

Q2 BLOCKING DEFECT B (wrong call-site inventory): the brief claims five call sites of the predicate, with plan_cmd.py as a PLAN-side one. Measured: plan_cmd.py never calls it (grep count 0). Only THREE files call it -- wrappers/preflight.sh:44, wrappers/finalize_merge.sh:160, gate/__init__.py:810.

ORCHESTRATOR-DISCOVERED, INDEPENDENT PRE-EXISTING DEFECT (not caused by this WP): wrappers/merge.sh:37 and gate/qoder_security.py:1012 do NOT use the hardened predicate at all -- they test the literal path fragment '/.worktrees/'. That is precisely the abandoned approach documented as wrong by test_verdict_does_not_depend_on_directory_name. Consequence measured today, before any change of mine: the path /Users/admin/vibe/agentic-loop-main-codex-merge/docs/plans/.../WP.status.json does not contain '/.worktrees/', so merge.sh and qoder_security ACCEPT it while preflight/finalize/gate REFUSE it. INV-5 (single authority) is therefore already violated in the current tree.

Q3: E10 as written would write git.target_branch into a WP fixture, producing a schema-invalid object, so it could fail for the wrong reason; it must use a legal PLAN status or an explicit declared-target input. E9/M-8 cannot catch the coordinated two-anchor move, so a coordinated-move attack test is required.

D7 FATAL, ORCHESTRATOR-REPRODUCED: the rev3 anchor is itself caller-controlled. XDG_CONFIG_HOME comes from the caller's environment, so `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/evil agentic ...` with /tmp/evil/agentic_loop/policy.toml declaring feat/evil resolves the anchor to an attacker-chosen file that is outside any git worktree and therefore PASSES E9b. Reproduced: the probe resolved /tmp/evil/agentic_loop/policy.toml, read 'feat/evil', and the worktree check answered False. This is precisely the A22 caller-declared-fact family that the predicate's own docstring rejects -- rev3 believed it had escaped that family and had not.

D8 (orchestrator-reproduced): scope self-contradiction returned in a new form -- merge.sh and qoder_security.py are now in BOTH allowed_paths and forbidden_paths, and the brief body still permits editing them while the recorded literal_defect decision reserves them for a separate WP. Additionally scope.decisions.existing_tests still calls the 17 guards 'read-only', contradicting INV-4's premise-preserving-rewrite rule.

D9 (orchestrator-reproduced): INV-3 conjunct 3 requires comparing git-common-dir against 'the repository owning the anchor', but INV-1b specifies the anchor lives outside any repository -- so it has no git-common-dir. The brief contradicts itself; a trusted repository identity must come from somewhere else.
D10: M-2 and M-2b both require 'E7 must turn red', but rev3 no longer defines E7 (it was replaced during the E9/E10/E11 rewrite). Two DoD items are therefore unexecutable as written.
D11: tests cannot relocate the anchor via XDG_CONFIG_HOME once that variable is removed from the production path; fixtures need internal dependency injection or a mockable path resolver instead.

Q1 mostly ACCEPT: the withdrawal was judged honest -- INV-1b clause 3 denies the trust boundary explicitly, E10/M-7's recasting as structural correctness is legitimate, and section 8 is specific enough to stop re-litigation. One incomplete spot: E1 still required an out-of-repo policy file, contradicting section 6's ban (D11).

Q3 FATAL, orchestrator-reproduced: rev4 keyed the predicate on PLAN git.target_branch, which is main. Measured here: ZERO worktrees hold main (git worktree list --porcelain | grep -c 'branch refs/heads/main$' = 0), and the authoritative status does not exist on main at all (git cat-file -e main:.../WP-01.status.json fails) while it does exist on the integration branch, held by this very checkout. rev4 would therefore fail-closed immediately with 'no checkout holds target_branch' -- trading the physical-location deadlock for a branch-lifecycle deadlock. USER DECISION: switch the basis to the integration branch, PLAN git.base_branch (D10).

Q2/Q4: M-2 was repointed from the deleted E7 to E3, but E3 is 'same repo, wrong branch' and would still be refused by INV-3 clause 2 after removing the common-dir comparison, so M-2 could not turn it red -- not load-bearing (D12). INV-5 had no acceptance test, only a DoD self-check. The brief said three call sites in section 1 and five in section 7. status forbidden_paths banned merge.sh and qoder_security.py while brief section 6 allowed them (D13). M-7 did not pin WHICH field is misread. INV-1b's no-fallback half and INV-5 had no guarding mutation.

rev5 fixes all of it: basis switched to base_branch with the measurement recorded; E1 uses a legal PLAN fixture; E7 restored as a dedicated cross-repository node with M-2 repointed at it; E12 added for INV-5 with M-12 guarding it; M-11 added to guard the no-fallback rule; M-7 now names WP status's own git.base_branch as the misread field; scope unified on five call sites in both the brief and this status; the duplicated topo-brief-r3 record merged.

Q1/Q3 directionally ACCEPT: the withdrawal is honest and keying on the integration branch is the right basis -- the consultant independently confirmed the integration branch is held by this linked worktree and carries the status while main has no holder and lacks the file.

D14 FATAL, orchestrator-reproduced: INV-3 clause 1 still used rev1's single-path-component check forbidding '/', but the real base_branch is plan/2026-10-15-status-source-topology, which contains '/'. The spec would reject its own authoritative branch and still fail closed, so rev5 did NOT lift the deadlock. The fixture names in E1/E3/E10 (plan/x, plan/y, plan/authoritative) were all illegal too. git check-ref-format --branch accepts the real name. Fix: validate by git's own ref syntax, and carry path safety as an implementation constraint -- the branch name is only ever string-compared against git worktree list --porcelain output, never concatenated into a path.

D15: M-2 still was not load-bearing. Candidates are enumerated by running git worktree list in the repository resolved FROM THE JUDGED PATH, so a foreign repository's worktree can never enter the candidate set; INV-3 clause 3 was therefore redundant and E7 could not go red. The consultant offered the smaller fix and the orchestrator took it: delete clause 3, E7 and M-2, and record that cross-repository confusion is excluded by the enumeration source itself.

D16: M-11 needed E9's fixture to contain a LIVE main holder, or adding a 'main' fallback merely turns 'unresolved' into 'no holder' -- still fail-closed, so E9 would not go red for wrongful acceptance. Premise added to E9.

D17: wording and stale values -- section 2 still said git.target_branch is not a trust boundary; section 1 still claimed three call sites; status scope notes literal_defect/wp02_split still said those two files were forbidden, contradicting allowed_paths and scope_rev5. All corrected; the stale notes are explicitly marked SUPERSEDED.

Also adopted from r5: section 8 no longer claims the integration branch 'disappears' after the plan merges (git merge does not necessarily delete it); it now says a merged plan's status no longer enters these gates whether or not the branch is kept.

substantiation: Q1: the withdrawal is complete and honest. INV-1b clause 3 denies that git.base_branch is a trust boundary, section 8 names the undefended actors and cites D7, and E10/M-7's structural-correctness recasting only prevents an implementation from reading the WP's own same-named field into a self-reference. No surviving requirement depends on an immovable trust root, and no environment variable, out-of-repo policy file or anchor was reintroduced.

Q2: E7 and M-2 are fully deleted from the normative text with no dangling reference. Surviving sets are E1-E6/E8/E9/E10/E12 and M-1/M-3/M-4/M-5/M-6/M-7/M-11/M-12, matching the DoD exactly. Every invariant has coverage: INV-1 by E1-E3, INV-1b by E9/E10, INV-2 by E2/E4, INV-2b by E5, INV-3 by E3/E6, INV-4 by E8, INV-5 by E12. The enumeration baseline is implementable -- resolve the repository from the judged path, run git worktree list --porcelain there -- so a foreign repository's worktree cannot be a candidate and dropping the common-dir comparison is the correct reduction.

Q3: independently measured -- the only holder is the linked worktree at /Users/admin/vibe/agentic-loop-main-codex-merge on plan/2026-10-15-status-source-topology, the PLAN/WP status exists on that integration branch and not on main, and git accepts the slashed name. Keying on PLAN git.base_branch with git check-ref-format validation and a unique live holder chosen from the judged repository's registered worktrees leaves no remaining conjunct that would reject the real layout. No phase-aware switching is needed because a MERGED plan's status no longer enters these gates.

Q4: each mutation turns its named test red through a specific witness -- M-1 stale-specific, M-3 name-validation, M-4 E1's self-proving linked layout, M-5 E3's wrong-branch witness, M-6 the existing caller-env tests, M-7 the legal WP git.base_branch set against the PLAN basis, M-11 the live main holder in E9 producing a wrongful acceptance, M-12 the five-call-site static assertion. All independently applicable, with no mutation needing another to go red, and the specific witnesses plus fixture premises prevent incidental greening via no-holder, schema-invalid or missing-branch.

Three non-blocking wording slips were named and the orchestrator fixed them without another round: the opening line still said three call sites, section 2 still said the integration branch 'disappears', and M-3 still said 8 name forms (now 12 negative).
